question: 24 tiles; orange box = the note detector's box at its exact size (1-13: every half note written from a too-wide box on a black-class box; 14-24: wide boxes at random). Which numbered boxes are on a real notehead?
verbatim: 6 of the orange boxes are actual notes nothing else is. I feel like many of those should have been ink that was already claimed and most of the boxes are just poorly sized or poorly placed boxes...
answer: 6 of the 24 boxes are on actual notes; the other 18 are not. He did not say which six.
ours: The cutting agent's own look also found six 'one head' boxes: tiles 4, 8, 10, 12, 13, 23 -- the count matches, the identity is NOT confirmed by Sean. His two hypotheses, to be traced not assumed: (1) much of the ink under the 18 should already have been claimed by a page-wide reader (slur, stem, beam, ledger line, tremolo, dynamic) before a head box could take it; (2) most of these boxes are poorly sized or placed. By the record, 7 of tiles 1-13 were made by our own split / rescue steps.
